author: Mark Atwood
text:
STATE 2026-11-24, 13 of 19. Everything still open needs either a decision
of Mark's or a front end that does not exist yet, so this is where the
epic stops without input:

- .8 (ACME DNS-01) stays in progress for one reason only: .8.1, RFC 2136
  with a TSIG key, is the last of §5.2's three DNS methods. It is now
  labelled `human`, because its own description asks the question Mark
  has to answer: an operator who runs their own nameserver can already
  write a three-line hook that calls nsupdate, which is the same protocol
  driven by a tool that is already installed and already correct. The
  bead buys not needing that hook, for 400 to 600 lines of DNS wire
  format and TSIG that mimid then owns. `hook` and `acme-dns` both ship.
- .7 (Matrix login) needs the Matrix front end, epic mimid-rvqk.
- .10 (XMPP SASL) needs the XMPP front end, epic mimid-wmdj.
- .15 and .16 (social login) need the provider's OAuth 2.1 AS, epic
  mimid-hb5z, whose .1 is a design note and is ready.
- .17 (createdBy names the asking credential) depends on .7: it needs
  AgentChat::CallerCtx to stop being an Id, which cascades through every
  ChatStore and JmapAccounts method in backend.rs and their delegations
  to a MemoryBackend whose CallerCtx is fixed at Id. Recorded in full on
  the bead, including the three approaches that do not work.

WHAT THE AUDIT OF THE SHIPPED HALF FOUND. Reading every section of
docs/design/frontend-auth.md against the code turned up one real gap,
filed and fixed as .19: nothing read the certificate's own notAfter, so
§5.4's expiry warnings did not exist and renewal was measured from the
certificate file's age against an assumed 90 days. §7.2's two certificate
log rows were unmet with it and are now met. Everything else checked out:
decision A9's public-listener WARN is in tls::warn_if_public with its own
test, and §7.1's unauthenticated-connection cap is IRC-only on purpose,
since an HTTP request has no "connection waiting to log in" (the HTTPS
listener has its own handshake cap in the `https` module instead).
